definitions.gloss: door-to-door inquiry, canvassing for information, investigation by questioning
definitions.explanation: The act of going around asking people for information, especially by police investigating a crime. A standard part of detective work in Japanese crime fiction and news reporting.

examples.japanese: {刑事|けいじ}が{聞|き}き{込|こ}みに{回|まわ}る。
examples.english: The detective goes around conducting inquiries.

examples.japanese: {近所|きんじょ}で{聞|き}き{込|こ}み{調査|ちょうさ}を{行|おこな}った。
examples.english: They conducted door-to-door inquiries in the neighborhood.

examples.japanese: {聞|き}き{込|こ}みの{結果|けっか}、{事件|じけん}{当日|とうじつ}に{不審|ふしん}な{人物|じんぶつ}を{見|み}たという{証言|しょうげん}が{得|え}られた。
examples.english: As a result of the door-to-door inquiries, they obtained a testimony that a suspicious person was seen on the day of the incident.

notes:
USAGE NOTE:
Strongly associated with police investigations. Very commonly heard in crime dramas, mystery novels, and news reports. The verb form is {聞|き}き{込|こ}みをする.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {聞|き}き{込|こ}みをする (conduct inquiries)
- {聞|き}き{込|こ}みに{回|まわ}る (go around asking questions)
- {聞|き}き{込|こ}み{調査|ちょうさ} (inquiry-based investigation)
- {聞|き}き{込|こ}み{捜査|そうさ} (investigation through questioning)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {取材|しゅざい}: news-gathering, reporting (journalistic context)
- {尋問|じんもん}: interrogation (more formal, at the station)
